amendment.rationale: Development smoke v3 exposed asymmetric date/identity evidence metadata. Before any held-out evaluation, normalize proved row scope across the unchanged control tools and custom/Wren backends, and apply shared strict qualifier checks. All 15 selected groups and 45 excluded groups retain their original membership; prompts, questions and reference labels are unchanged. This binds the corrected source without rescoring or validating earlier runs.

changes.rationale: The same four financial tools, clarification/proposal semantics, scoped queries and one model call remain. Existing trusted dates and identities now carry machine-owned scope metadata for the shared validator/scorer. No tool, retrieval ability, model-visible tag inference or subgroup capability is added.

Custom and actual Wren query evidence now shares validated period/identity metadata from compiler plans or supported parsed ASTs. Missing or ambiguous scope fails closed, including monthly grain and calculation provenance. The shared model prompts, query/retrieval capabilities, threshold and question membership remain unchanged; conservative unsupported SQL scopes are disclosed integration limits.

limits: R0 formal CLARIFY versus expected BLOCK remains a disclosed protocol limitation, not a harmful action.
Conservative unsupported SQL grain or ambiguous calculation operands may withhold valid answers; qualifier provenance is not complete economic-semantic or prose verification.
Smoke v3 and both pilots remain diagnostic/ineligible. A separately named corrected development smoke precedes final freezing and held-out evaluation.

notes: Supplementary common-answerable subgroup; the whole-benchmark six-family macro remains primary. No winner is selected by this analyzer.
All recorded errors and blocks remain in subgroup denominators; missing and unscheduled episodes are separate. No candidate was selected using observed correctness.
The fixed held-out subgroup has 12 questions in six scenario groups, covering financial and entry families only. Repetitions and paraphrases are not independent observations.
Observed-family macro averages only families with measurements; it is not a six-family macro. Always read family counts and missing coverage.

Paired intervals use scenario-group blocks within families and are exploratory, unadjusted for multiple comparisons, and unstable with so few groups. A zero-width empirical interval does not imply certainty.

Primary completion, verified ledger-and-corpus fingerprint, full subgroup coverage, and matching membership-source hashes are required for comparative eligibility. Any hard-gate violation anywhere in a route remains disqualifying.

Changed source files are diagnostic unless an explicit reviewed amendment binds exact definition/comparison hashes. Legacy route-only amendments cannot waive baseline changes; a version-2 metadata amendment must bind both baseline and route hashes and preserve membership. Question-source changes cannot be waived.
This postprocessor reuses the preserved primary scores after checking raw outcome identity and metadata. It does not silently rescore using a later reference or rubric version.

An adjacent post-run validity notice supersedes mechanical completion/integrity eligibility. A notice with an unverified run/report binding also forces diagnostic status; it never silently repairs or replaces original scores.
